text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand, which improves readability for everyone on the team. When developers refactor, they reorganize and simplify code, but the program's behavior stays exactly the same. This practice is important because it helps reduce technical debt—the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly or poorly. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their projects healthy and easier to maintain over time. In short, refactoring makes code better on the inside while keeping it working the same on the outside.
